title: Is a static main menu better or a live one? Testing out both and would love some feedback
author: fapfap_ahh
selftext: First is the static menu. Second is the live menu. For the live menu I may change the scenes that play

replies.author: fapfap_ahh
replies.body: Thank you! I think do need to find a better scene though. Maybe a mix of day and night with an Aurora

replies.author: fapfap_ahh
replies.body:
Question for you on the live menu. 

Should the camera view stay fixed like it is (looking at one spot) or move around to explore and change day/night + weather?

Currently it transitions through 3 different scenes but it could be one complete "transitional" piece

replies.author: theplushpairing
replies.body: Have it change slightly/interact with the cursor, but the main goal of the screen is for people to pick the menu item so don’t overdo it… or do. How epic would it be if the whole game was inside the menu screen lol

replies.author: fapfap_ahh
replies.body:
Good advice! I'll note that for the next iteration.

I really want to do something where some of the game is loaded in the live menu, you hit new or load game and as the rest loads in the background:

* The camera walks you through the live menu scene to your start position
* A wolf hunts a deer or some similar event in the distance
* Your player starts getting ready, then it starts you off.


All seamless hopefully.

comments.author: Unlikely_Perspective
comments.body: Yep I agree with live here.

replies.author: fapfap_ahh
replies.body: Thank you for the feedback sir

comments.author: fapfap_ahh
comments.body: If anyone needs the skill / tool on how to do this with Claude + Unity let me know I'll post a reply with it :)

comments.author: MVPof93
comments.body: Live pulls me into the game better

comments.author: darkoblivion000
comments.body: Definitely live. But you could also make the spear into a live menu too. I’m imagining Skyrim type loading screens where you get a closeup of the object showing all the details as it slowly pans or moves up the screen. That felt pretty nice too

replies.author: fapfap_ahh
replies.body:
The spear has some effects and animations, the first part was a static image so it didn't show it, I should've added that in the preview. 

Rings move around off it, it moves with your mouse position. But it didn't feel right for some reason. 

Right now the new menu starts off with that spear background and fades into the live scene

comments.author: wewerecreaturres
comments.body: I’m more of a live menu kinda guy myself, but could see static working with some juice

replies.author: fapfap_ahh
replies.body: I can see that for sure, it needs the right touch. I'd probably pay one of my UI/UX friends to help me design it better if I went that way, but it seems like the live one creates more immersion

comments.author: fapfap_ahh
comments.body: Good eye! Thank you! I can add this to my next iteration.

comments.author: wllmsaccnt
comments.body: The live definitely looks better, but the important question is if there is a difference in how long they take to load. At an extra 3-5 seconds for a game I'd play more than a few times, I'd probably prefer the first menu. I might oggle an animated menu screen the first time I open a game, but its usually just a distraction after that.

replies.author: fapfap_ahh
replies.body: The load time is within margin of error, it's actually pre-recorded so it's just videos that stream and transition lol. I'm running benchmarks on a proper pre-baked scene next which could affect load times noticeablely. On my mid tier machine I didn't notice any change at all with the video version.

comments.author: Stunning-Relation564
comments.body: live menu, but less live, if that makes sense?

replies.author: fapfap_ahh
replies.body: Basically less going on so it's not distracting, right?

comments.author: Ukawok92
comments.body: Live. Maybe a bit subtler snowfall.

comments.author: Prestigious_Fee_2468
comments.body: Depends on the performance effects, lower spec devices will run into issues

replies.author: fapfap_ahh
replies.body: It's basically just a pre recorded movie that plays so should be negligible in performance. I was looking at a pre baked scene which would have an impact but benchmarking that first

replies.author: Prestigious_Fee_2468
replies.body: Any plans on making it a setting that switches them? Some will like one while others will like the other and this will be a good way to appeal to both sides lol

replies.author: fapfap_ahh
replies.body:
Good question. Right now there's quite a few graphics settings that you can fine tune before/after selecting a quality tier so I was hoping not to add a ton but maybe not a bad idea to section them and add this one.

I do need to add a few more settings like sliders for motion blur intensity anyways (it already has an on/off)

replies.author: Prestigious_Fee_2468
replies.body: Usually when I play games I go to settings increase aiming sensitivity, turn off a number of settings to give my playthroughs more excitement, motion blurr with high sensitivity settings is a pain in the a... Lol but right now I'm getting into gdevelop5 I'm thinking of doing a simple small game that's not very complicated to make just to publish one, my issue is I'll get into one project then work on another until I want to make much bigger projects

comments.author: Ok_Championship1836
comments.body:
https://i.redd.it/s3vedes0zbyh1.png

Brother, left red lines looks very AI (probably Opus). I see it a lot in my projects, when I miss UI specification.

replies.author: Ok_Championship1836
replies.body: same for second screen. I bet this red line isn't intended. What do you think guys?

replies.author: fapfap_ahh
replies.body: That's a good point, it does look AI-ish, and it definitely is opus 5.5. I'll take note of that and get some help from my UI friend for a fix up there, thanks!
